To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified an SLC45A1 deletion as the cause of albinism in a Bullmastif.
we identified an SLC45A 2 gene variant in a single Bullmastiff that causes oculocutaneus albinism.

we detected a single base pair deletion in exon 5 of the SLC4A2 gene in the Bullmastiff with OCA, that this mutation has never been described before, and that it perfectly cosegregated with the phenotype within the available family members.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the causative variant for a Bullmastiff affected with oculocoutaneous albinism.
the identification of the molecular basis of oculocutaneously albinism in a Bullmastuff.
a new SLC45A 2 variant that causes oculocutancous albinism in dogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SLC45a2 is a major contributor to oculocutaneus albinism in dogs, and that this gene has a major role in oculocuteneous albinism in humans.
the Bullmastiff oculocutaneously albino dog has a novel SLC45A 2 deletion mutation that causes OCA4.
SLC45a2 variants cause oculocoutaneous albinism (OCA) in dogs and that this phenotype is caused by a single base deletion (c.1287delc) in the SLC 45a2 gene in a single dog.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel SLC45A 2 variant in a highly inbred Bullmastiff with albinism.
the SLC45a2 gene is the most important gene in the pigmentation process.
this is the third SLC45A gene variant reported in dog that causes oculocutaneus albinism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same gene is responsible for oculocutaneus albinism in different dog breeds and the same gene can be responsible in humans and dogs.
the Bullmastiff with albinism is homozygous for a single base deletion (c.1287del C) in SLC45A 2, and this variant has not been previously described in any other dog breed.
SLC45a2 is the most frequently mutated gene in dogs with oculocuteaneous albinism and that it should therefore be tested first.
